tasks.title: Adopt contract units and entity IDs in CADCraft
tasks.rationale: CADCraft stores units in an INSUNITS header variable and identifies entities with Handle(u64). The contract already provides Unit with exact conversions and EntityId, which is the same u64 with validation. Unit mistakes are the most expensive class of CAD bug.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and INSUNITS mapping round-trip through the DXF reader/writer for millimetre and inch drawings.
EntityId is introduced for new code and Handle converts to it losslessly; no persisted file changes meaning.
Existing CADCraft tests still pass.
required_tests: cargo test -p cadcraft-doc
cargo test -p cadcraft-dxf
tasks.rollback: EntityId is a type alias over u64 at first, so reverting is a type change with no data migration.

tasks.title: Install and wire cargo-audit and cargo-deny
tasks.rationale: Neither cargo-audit, cargo-deny nor cargo-license is installed on this host, so the advisory state of roughly 1,085 resolved packages across the two applications is unknown. A review cannot report a clean bill of health it never measured.
acceptance_criteria: cargo-audit and cargo-deny are available and their versions recorded.
deny.toml exists for CADCraft, matching SolidCraft's existing policy.
cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources runs for both applications and its output is recorded.
A CI guard fails when opencascade* or cadrum enters a shipping dependency graph.
required_tests: cargo deny check on both applications
tasks.last_error: Blocked by the toolchain: cargo-audit, cargo-deny and cargo-license are not installed on this host, and installing global tooling is outside the authorized scope of a coding session.
tasks.rollback: Removing deny.toml and the CI step restores the previous state; no application code is touched.

tasks.title: Implement cad_contract::Kernel for solidcraft-kernel behind a feature flag
tasks.rationale: This is the milestone that turns a contract into an integration: the production kernel would implement the shared trait without changing behaviour, and a test would prove the contract describes the kernel actually shipped.
acceptance_criteria: cad-contract is an optional dependency of apps/solidcraft/crates/kernel, feature off by default.
Kernel is implemented by delegating to the existing Body API; KernelError maps onto the contract taxonomy.
A test builds a box both ways and compares volume from the contract path with the kernel's own answer.
No existing public signature changes; the existing test suite passes unchanged.
required_tests: cargo test -p solidcraft-kernel --features cad-contract
tasks.rollback: Delete the adapter module and the optional dependency; the feature is off by default, so no released behaviour depends on it.

tasks.title: Decide the OpenCASCADE licence path (owner gate G1)
tasks.rationale: opencascade-rs is LGPL-2.1 and cadrum statically links LGPL-2.1 OCCT behind an MIT wrapper. Neither is in a shipping graph today, but the decision determines whether OCCT is ever usable and what the CI guard must forbid.
acceptance_criteria: An owner decision is recorded as an ADR: exclude OCCT, dynamic-link it with relink rights, or relicense the product.
engineering/manifest/repositories.json and docs/license-inventory.md reflect the decision.
If exclusion is chosen, a CI guard proves opencascade* and cadrum cannot enter a shipping graph.
tasks.last_error: Requires an owner decision (G1 in docs/roadmap.md); an engineering session must not choose a distribution licence on the owner's behalf.
tasks.rollback: No code change; the ADR can be superseded by a later ADR.

tasks.title: Add import budgets and cancellation to SolidCraft IO
tasks.rationale: Untrusted CAD files are the primary attack surface, and SolidCraft's IO lacks the size, entity and zip-entry caps that CADCraft already has. A 3MF import can exhaust memory or disk without a bound today.
acceptance_criteria: Maximum file size, entity count, triangle count, zip entry count and uncompressed size are enforced and configurable.
An import can be cancelled and returns a structured error rather than hanging.
A test feeds a zip-bomb-shaped 3MF and a truncated STEP file and asserts a clean error.
required_tests: cargo test -p solidcraft-io
tasks.rollback: Budgets are additive checks; raising a limit or removing the check restores prior behaviour.

tasks.title: Audit the MCP loopback control port
tasks.rationale: CADCraft's MCP backend talks to the app over a loopback control port that any local process can reach. The security review flagged this as unaudited, and MCP is the second attack surface after file parsing.
acceptance_criteria: The port binds only to 127.0.0.1 and rejects non-loopback peers.
Requests are authenticated or validated so another local process cannot drive the editor.
Malformed and hostile requests are tested and rejected without affecting the document.
required_tests: an integration test that sends a malformed request and asserts a clean refusal
tasks.rollback: Document the finding and revert any binding change; the default remains loopback.

tasks.title: Run the SolidCraft kernel test suite on a larger machine
tasks.rationale: 5,884 tests exist and not one was executed here; a single crate took 8 min 22 s and 2.56 GB RSS against a 7.4 GB host with swap largely consumed. Until they run, every SolidCraft capability claim remains advertised, not verified.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p solidcraft-kernel completes on a machine with at least 16 GB RAM.
Pass, fail and ignored counts are recorded in engineering/quality/tests.json.
Any failure is triaged into a task with a reproduction, not ignored.
required_tests: cargo test -p solidcraft-kernel
tasks.last_error: Host memory: one crate build peaked at 2.56 GB RSS with only ~1.3 GB available at audit time; the test suite is larger than the build.
tasks.rollback: No changes are made by running tests.

tasks.title: Generate one combined third-party notice bundle
tasks.rationale: Each application ships its own notice material, but a combined distribution has no aggregated bundle. Apache-2.0 section 4(d) obligations must be met per distributed artifact, not per repository.
acceptance_criteria: A generated bundle lists name, version, licence and repository for every resolved dependency of both applications.
It includes both NOTICE files and the SolidCraft vendor patch notes.
Regeneration is a single documented command and the output is reviewed for GPL/LGPL entries.
required_tests: the generator fails when a dependency has no licence field
tasks.rollback: The bundle is generated output; deleting it changes nothing else.

tasks.title: Put the workspace root under version control
tasks.rationale: No Git repository exists at the workspace root, so the contract crates, manifests, docs and reports have no history and no recovery path. That is a data-loss risk, and it means every evidence record is unattributable to a revision.
acceptance_criteria: A repository exists at the workspace root with nested checkouts ignored, or the owner explicitly declines and the reason is recorded.
target/, engineering/state/ and the 39 MB reference archive are either ignored or committed deliberately.
The first commit contains the manifests, docs and crates, and the scanner's state is reproducible from it.
required_tests: atlas-eng scan --write produces the same fingerprint after checkout
evidence: engineering/state/scan.json will show `no Git metadata` for platform crates
tasks.rollback: Initializing a repository is additive; deleting .git would undo it. Do not run it without the owner's agreement, because nested repositories would become embedded without a .gitignore policy.
